title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your assistant helped a student on Monday. On Wednesday the same student starts a new session, and the program sends the model only the instructions and the new question. What does the model know about Monday?

options.text: Everything, because the model keeps its own memory of past chats
Nothing, because only what the program sends is in its context
A summary, because models store a short digest of each chat
Everything, as long as the context window is large enough

items.stem: An agent's fixed instructions and tool descriptions take 2,000 tokens, and the question takes 100. The agent makes three model calls: call 1 sends the fixed part and the question; a tool result of 500 tokens is added before call 2; a second tool result of 400 tokens is added before call 3. Ignore the tokens the model writes. How many input tokens are sent in total across the three calls?
You want the assistant to know that a student passed laser cutter training, so it can greet them correctly next semester. Which design is best?

options.text: Save the whole chat in notes and send all of it each time
Save a small training-status record and load it at session start
Rely on a larger context window to carry it over to next semester
Put every student's training status in the instructions for all calls

items.stem: In one or two sentences, why is it usually better to retrieve a few relevant chunks of the manuals for each question than to put all the manuals into the context?
The assistant told a student that a machine was free on Friday, using a booking summary it saved in its notes two weeks ago. The machine had been booked since. What design mistake caused this?

options.text: It copied a changing fact into notes instead of looking it up
It saved too few tokens of notes to keep the answer current
It used retrieval where it should have used a bigger window
It cleared old tool results before the model finished reading them
